q: In workshop accounts, process wastage is best defined as

options.A: Material lost during conversion of raw material into finished components
options.B: Loss detected only during annual stock verification
options.C: Theft of finished components from the shop floor
options.D: Shortage of tools issued to individual artisans

q: A shortage in workshop stores differs from process wastage because it

options.A: Is detected on physical verification against book balances
options.B: Is recovered by remelting the scrap
options.D: Is credited back to the work order

q: Cuttings, turnings and borings in a machine shop are examples of

options.A: Theft losses requiring police reporting
options.B: Recoverable scrap arising as process wastage
options.D: Surplus material returned to stores

q: Wastage within the prescribed percentage limits is normally

options.A: Recovered from the wages of the shop artisans
options.B: Carried forward as a suspense balance indefinitely
options.C: Charged to the personal account of the shop in-charge
options.D: Written off under sanction of the competent authority per the Schedule of Powers

q: Wastage exceeding the prescribed limits requires

options.A: No action since it is treated as normal loss
options.B: Automatic credit to the work order
options.C: Investigation and sanction of a higher authority
options.D: Recovery from the stores depot officer

q: Shortages noticed during stock verification of workshop stores are reported through

options.A: A gate pass
options.B: A work order
options.D: A job card

q: A survey committee in the workshop context is generally composed of representatives of

options.A: Only the accounts department
options.B: The railway board and the ministry
options.D: The mechanical, stores and accounts departments

q: Survey committees are appointed to examine

options.A: New work orders received by the workshop
options.B: Unserviceable, obsolete or surplus stores and cases of loss
options.C: The annual production targets of the shop
options.D: Leave applications of workshop staff

q: Loss of workshop material due to theft must be

options.A: Reported to the police and a loss statement prepared
options.B: Concealed to avoid audit objection
options.C: Adjusted against the next material indent
options.D: Written off by the shop artisan concerned

q: Sanction for write-off of losses in workshops is governed by

options.A: The personal discretion of the foreman
options.B: The seniority of the store keeper
options.C: The value of scrap sold in the previous year
options.D: The Schedule of Powers delegating financial authority

q: Melting loss in a foundry is an example of

options.A: Avoidable shortage
options.B: Theft of raw material
options.D: Clerical error in stock records

q: Scrap generated during manufacture is credited

options.A: At full issue price to the supplier
options.B: To the personal ledger of the artisan
options.C: At its scrap value, reducing the cost of the work order
options.D: As miscellaneous revenue of the railway board

q: Prescribed wastage percentages for workshop operations are fixed by

options.A: The individual artisan
options.B: The scrap purchaser
options.C: The railway administration based on experience and trials
options.D: The trade union of the shop

q: Loss of small tools in a workshop is normally charged to

options.A: The capital account of the workshop
options.B: Shop overhead or on-cost
options.D: The provident fund of the staff

q: When a shortage is found, the first step is to

options.A: Write it off immediately
options.B: Recheck records and investigate the cause
options.D: Suspend the store keeper

q: Loss statements of workshops are submitted to

options.A: The canteen committee
options.B: The scrap contractor
options.D: The accounts department for scrutiny and sanction processing

q: Unavoidable wastage differs from avoidable wastage in that it

options.A: Needs no sanction at all
options.B: Is always recovered from staff
options.D: Is inherent in the process and occurs despite normal care

q: Material damaged in transit to the workshop is treated as

options.A: Process wastage of the receiving shop
options.B: Scrap credited to the work order
options.C: A shortage or loss for which claim may lie against the carrier
options.D: A normal stores receipt

q: The cost of material wasted in manufacture is borne by

options.A: The railway minister fund
options.B: The work order for which the material was issued
options.D: The succeeding financial year

q: Standard wastage allowances for repetitive workshop jobs help in

options.A: Eliminating the need for stock verification
options.B: Avoiding quality inspection
options.C: Comparing actual wastage with norms and detecting excess
options.D: Increasing the issue price of material

q: Surplus material returned from a shop to the stores depot is

options.A: Sold immediately as scrap
options.B: Destroyed in the presence of a committee
options.C: Credited to the work order at issue price
options.D: Charged to the next work order automatically

q: Loss of expensive metals in workshops is minimised by

options.A: Issuing them without any record
options.B: Writing them off every month
options.C: Storing them in the open yard
options.D: Collecting and remelting the scrap and sweepings

q: Shortage in finished stock of a shop is primarily the responsibility of

options.A: The railway board
options.B: The audit department
options.D: The shop in-charge having custody of the stock

q: Credit for scrap recovered during manufacture

options.A: Increases the unit cost of production
options.B: Is ignored in cost accounts
options.C: Reduces the net cost of the work order
options.D: Is paid to the artisans as incentive

q: Condemnation of workshop plant and machinery is recommended by

options.A: The machine operator alone
options.B: A survey committee after examining its condition
options.D: The production planning cell

q: Loss due to fire in a workshop store must be

options.A: Adjusted by inflating the next indent
options.B: Reported, surveyed and written off under competent sanction
options.C: Borne by the insurance agent personally
options.D: Left out of the accounts

q: If a loss is caused by negligence of a railway servant, the administration may

options.A: Ignore it as a normal risk
options.B: Charge it to passenger earnings
options.D: Order recovery of the loss from the person responsible

q: Periodic stock verification in workshops is conducted to

options.A: Increase the production targets
options.B: Fix the duty roster of artisans
options.D: Detect shortages, excesses and deterioration of stores

q: Obsolete workshop stores are disposed of after

options.A: Survey and declaration as obsolete by a committee
options.B: Keeping them for ten more years
options.D: Mixing them with new stock

q: Shrinkage of timber in the saw mill is a form of

options.A: Process wastage
options.B: Theft
options.D: Finished product

q: Defective castings that cannot be used are treated as

options.A: Finished stock
options.B: Good components after painting
options.D: Foundry loss credited as scrap after remelting

q: Scrap leaving the workshop for sale must be covered by

options.A: Only a verbal instruction
options.B: The artisan job card
options.C: A gate pass authorising its removal
options.D: A passenger ticket

q: Chemical loss in electroplating shops is classified as

options.A: Process wastage of the plating operation
options.B: Shortage of finished goods
options.D: Excess of production

q: Oil and grease consumed on machines beyond normal lubrication is viewed as

options.A: Process wastage to be watched against norms
options.B: Capital expenditure
options.D: Scrap for sale

q: An annual review of wastage percentages in workshops is useful to

options.A: Revise norms in light of actual experience
options.B: Abolish stock verification
options.D: Fix staff salaries

q: Patterns and dies that become unserviceable are

options.A: Repaired indefinitely
options.B: Surveyed, condemned and written off under sanction
options.C: Issued to artisans for home use
options.D: Charged to passenger revenue

q: Material found excess on stock verification is

options.A: Ignored
options.B: Taken on charge through an adjustment entry
options.D: Written off immediately

q: Wastage of costly non-ferrous metals is controlled by

options.A: Issuing them in bulk without weighing
options.B: Weighing issues and returns and recovering all scrap
options.C: Writing off the full quantity issued
options.D: Storing them with general scrap

q: A loss statement must show

options.A: Nature, quantity, value of loss and the circumstances
options.B: Only the name of the store keeper
options.C: The production target for next year
options.D: The scrap sale proceeds

q: Write-off of a loss does not

options.A: Absolve the need to fix responsibility where negligence is involved
options.B: Need any documentation
options.D: Need entry in the accounts
